root.title: Apply the Pest patch independently of temporary-directory Git context
root.description:
Package: orbit-pest-setup-git-context
Revision: 1
Root key: pest-setup-git-context
Project: orbit
Repository: https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit
Source: [ORB-253 — Apply the Pest patch independently of temporary-directory Git context](https://linear.app/nckrtl/issue/ORB-253/apply-the-pest-patch-independently-of-temporary-directory-git-context)
Source UUID: `615603ac-f019-4dbc-b60e-bf343d76be6c`
Inspected baseline: clean primary `/home/nckrtl/orbit`, HEAD/local origin/main/fresh remote main `317de2b630f7e8febdc3f2a25a664e10d14a6beb` on 2026-09-13.
Parent: none
Depends on: none
Child order: fix-pest-setup-git-context (one executable child)

Objective: Composer's Pest setup applies its pinned patch independently of a writable temporary directory's Git context and reports patch failures without requiring an unnecessary reinstall.

Scope:

- In: `bin/pest-setup`, the existing `apps/e2e/tests/Unit/E2E/PestSetupTest.php` subprocess fixtures, and Pest setup recovery guidance in `docs/reference/implementation-loop.md`.
- Out: the pinned Pest version and patch contents, dependency upgrades, TIA selection/cache recovery, bootstrap scheduling, caller database isolation, live worktree repair, and new framework or orchestration surfaces.

Shared context:

- Read Orbit `AGENTS.md`, `apps/e2e/AGENTS.md`, accepted ADRs 0052 and 0054, and `docs/reference/implementation-loop.md`. Preserve private project/cache ownership and the current affected-TIA, Builder gate, and independent-review requirements.
- The native helper verifies version and patch hash, locks the selected vendor, accepts already-patched files, verifies upstream hashes, runs Git check/apply, and verifies output hashes. Both subprocesses use `sys_get_temp_dir()` as cwd. With TMPDIR below another repository root, Git skips all nine absolute patch targets at exit zero. The final hash guard refuses success but incorrectly requires reinstalling unchanged upstream packages.
- The published diagnosis attachment `1834a85a-0895-4fa1-8303-9ff1d8863d55` contains the unchanged-helper reproduction; bundle SHA-256 `c5886b5e3041290cc92e3729db16e5008f537412ba5652a46c25292fc58f8566`. Outside-Git and repository-root controls passed; a Git-subdirectory failed; moving only TMPDIR recovered the same fixture and a repeated run was idempotent. This is diagnosis, not candidate acceptance evidence.
- `PestSetupTest.php` already builds minimal Composer metadata, copies the installed patched package, reverses the pinned patch to upstream, invokes the real helper with Symfony Process, and covers repeat setup, modified upstream, unsupported versions, no Pest, and linked Pest checkouts. It also contains real Git repository/worktree construction for TIA identity. Extend this machinery; do not replace the helper with a test imitation.
- The upstream fixture reversal also currently runs from `sys_get_temp_dir()`. Establish and verify valid fixture inputs before setting the adversarial TMPDIR for the child under test. Fixture creation and verification must not silently share the context defect. The existing fake `.git` marker alone is not a real linked-worktree context.
- Use the smallest supported change that meets the contract. Keep existing hashes, locking, refusal rules, and ordinary success paths. Code-level Git invocation and diagnostic wording choices remain with the implementer.

Execution and isolation:

- This is opt-in Commander Tasks preparation, not legacy `.loop` planning. Use discovery without Incus: the issue concerns local automated Git/subprocess behavior, not managed-machine behavior. No browser validation is required; no UI changes are in scope.
- One fresh implementer delivers reviewable uncommitted setup, regression, and documentation changes. The retained reviewer reviews the exact submitted tree and creates one coherent commit after a pass. Corrections stay in that TaskRun; only one actor writes at a time. No implementer-created commit or separate documentation/preflight commit.
- Before kickoff, the coordinator binds the approved briefs and source issue to a clean registered isolated ORB-253 worktree, confirms exclusive ownership, and checks its project-local test configuration and generated caches. No worktree is assigned or created by this package. Unrelated main movement alone does not invalidate preparation; relevant contract/source changes require reconciliation.
- Launch project commands with no inherited Commander application environment or credentials, using the current `TaskProcessEnvironment::isolated()` boundary for the final gate and equivalent explicit clearing for other subprocesses. It retains an OS allowlist; omitted variables in a Symfony Process environment are otherwise inherited. Commander references: `docs/task-runtime.md`, “Project process environment,” and `app/Tasks/Runtime/TaskProcessEnvironment.php`.
- Each Composer project must load its own verified test settings and use only its intended disposable resources, with task-private app/cache/output paths where needed. Inspect effective own-dotenv and cached configuration, not only inherited values. Use disposable SQLite and no caller DB URL. Do not inject a blanket `APP_ENV=testing`: doing so disables CLI Boost during guidance checks. Let each project's supported configuration establish its environment.
- Use a task-private outside-repository TMPDIR for preparation and ordinary checks while the old helper exists. Adversarial test subprocesses must deliberately receive the Git-nested TMPDIR required by F1; do not sanitize that test input away. Keep sentinel repositories, synthetic packages, failure stubs, and any altered checksum bundle disposable; never mutate real vendors, the real pinned patch, Commander data, or live cache publications for a regression.
- Run Orbit Pest through its unfiltered TIA commands. Do not add file, filter, group, suite, or no-TIA selectors. Report unrelated red checks and unavailable proof to the coordinator without weakening assertions, clearing holds, or absorbing another repair. ORB-247 and ORB-252 remain separate.
root.acceptance_criteria:
Feature acceptance, in ORB-253 order:

- F1: The native hook exits zero with exact manifest-patched files when writable TMPDIR is outside Git, at a repository root, or below a real checkout or linked-worktree root, including paths with spaces.
- F2: Only the selected project's intended Pest installation and setup lock change. Another project's package, Composer locks, tracked/untracked sentinels, and the enclosing temporary repository's HEAD/index/status remain unchanged.
- F3: An exact-upstream installation retained after a failed attempt recovers through the native hook without dependency deletion/reinstall; repeating setup preserves verified patched files.
- F4: Nonzero patch execution and exit-zero non-application fail setup with an actionable patch-execution diagnostic, without requiring reinstall of unchanged upstream files or confusing them with modified packages.
- F5: Unsupported versions, changed patch checksums, modified package files, and linked upstream checkouts remain refused; supported already-patched and no-Pest installs still succeed.
- F6: Maintained setup guidance distinguishes execution failure from modified files and documents supported retry without unnecessary reinstall or cache deletion.

Coverage:

| Feature | Child criterion | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | T1 | V1, V2 |
| F2 | T2 | V1, V2 |
| F3 | T3 | V1, V2 |
| F4 | T4 | V1, V2 |
| F5 | T5 | V1–V3 |
| F6 | T6 | V4 |
| Complete outcome and scope | T1–T6 | V5, I1–I3 |

Final acceptance:

- I1: Inspect the exact accepted commit and the child's V1–V5 evidence against F1–F6. Require executed regression cases, preserved safeguards, matching documentation, and only scoped changes.
- I2: From the clean committed issue worktree, the Builder runs root `composer check` through the configured isolated final-command boundary. Require the existing repository-produced exact-head receipt with zero exits across all five Composer projects, not a prior worktree's bootstrap or gate receipt.
- I3: The retained independent final reviewer checks that same unchanged candidate, I2 receipt, and all acceptance evidence and returns an explicit pass. No automatic repeat of the whole gate is required without a concrete concern.

Completing the child does not alone complete the root. Reviewed publication, merge, actual-main recovery, incident clearance, and cleanup remain separate coordinator actions. All implementation checks above are future requirements, not passing preparation results.

children.title: Fix Pest setup Git-context handling and recovery advice
children.description:
Task key: fix-pest-setup-git-context
Kind: executable
Project: orbit
Parent: pest-setup-git-context
Depends on: none

Objective: Make native pinned-Pest setup insensitive to temporary-directory Git context, with trustworthy failure advice and executable regression coverage.

Scope: the root's exact helper, existing E2E unit-test file/fixtures, and maintained setup guidance; preserve every root exclusion. Keep setup, tests, and documentation in one reviewer-created commit.

Context:

- Inherit the root brief and published ORB-253 contract. Exercise the real `bin/pest-setup` entry point in disposable Composer projects, using the pinned manifest as the expected file-state authority.
- Reuse `pestSetupFixture()`, `runPestSetup()`, and the file's existing real Git/worktree setup patterns as appropriate. Real nested checkout/worktree contexts, full sentinel comparisons, failing/no-op Git processes, and checksum-corruption coverage are cases to add, not existing passing acceptance proof.
- Keep fixture construction valid independently of the TMPDIR under test. Perform any checksum mutation on a disposable copy of the unchanged setup bundle, and keep Git failure injection local to the test process.
- Choose a small native implementation. No new generic execution framework, dependency, TIA change, bootstrap redesign, or live recovery is needed.
children.acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance:

- T1: All F1 contexts produce the exact manifest-patched files through the native hook; the real Git-subdirectory regression detects the original defect. Covers F1.
- T2: Intended mutation stays within the selected package and lock; neighboring package, Composer locks, sentinels, and enclosing repository HEAD/index/status match their before-state. Covers F2.
- T3: The retained-upstream recovery case succeeds without reinstall and repeated setup leaves patched hashes unchanged. Covers F3.
- T4: Failing and no-op patch-process cases fail with accurate execution diagnostics and intact upstream hashes, distinct from the modified-package error. Covers F4.
- T5: Existing safety refusals and supported already-patched/no-Pest behavior remain; add the missing checksum case without changing the real pinned bundle. Covers F5.
- T6: The maintained setup section describes the observed failure distinction and supported retry accurately, without unnecessary reinstall/cache deletion. Covers F6.

Verification:

- V1: T1–T5; cwd assigned `apps/e2e`; `composer test:affected -- --log-junit=<private-output>/e2e.xml`; expected exit 0 and actual execution of the extended `tests/Unit/E2E/PestSetupTest.php` cases. Command and fixture machinery exist; the new cases are this task's work. If TIA does not execute the required cases, use supported unfiltered `composer test:affected -- --fresh --log-junit=<private-output>/e2e-fresh.xml` and retain its actual result.
- V2: T1–T5; inspect the V1 subprocess observations: exact argv/cwd/TMPDIR, upstream/patched hashes, sentinel and repository-state comparisons, failure exits, and diagnostic distinctions. The original Git-nested behavior must be rejected by the regression; retained failure/no-op and neighboring-package controls must remain meaningful. Use disposable before/after observations or a bounded temporary negative control; restore any temporary diagnostic changes before handoff. Evidence is to produce, not already passing.
- V3: T5 and affected-project quality; cwd assigned `apps/e2e`; `composer check`; expected exit 0. Existing command runs guidance, Rector, Pint, and PHPStan.
- V4: T6; cwd assigned repository root; `composer docs-lint`; expected exit 0, plus review the edited `docs/reference/implementation-loop.md` setup section against the tested results. Existing command; documentation change is to produce.
- V5: T1–T6 and scope; cwd assigned repository root; `git diff --check` and full intended-diff inspection; expected exit 0, only scoped changes, no leftover diagnostic mutation, and no implementer commit.

Outputs:

- Reviewable uncommitted helper, regression tests, and documentation. Yield after the assigned Commander handoff; the reviewer creates one clean commit only after an exact-tree pass.
- Evidence maps T1–T6 to exact commands, working directories, actual case results, exits, and retained logs. Keep failed/unrun checks, environment corrections, and any temporary changes/cleanup explicit.
- Distinguish isolated patch acceptance from complete bootstrap or actual-main recovery. Do not claim prior diagnosis or another issue's successful gate as this candidate's proof.

issue.title: Apply the Pest patch independently of temporary-directory Git context
issue.description:
Composer's Pest setup applies the pinned patch when a caller's writable temporary directory is inside another Git checkout, without requiring a dependency reinstall. On main `317de2b630f7e8febdc3f2a25a664e10d14a6beb`, a Git-subdirectory `TMPDIR` made both patch commands exit zero while skipping all nine files, so bootstrap failed in all five projects and incorrectly advised reinstalling unchanged upstream packages.

## Scope

* In: temporary-directory Git context and failure diagnostics in `bin/pest-setup`.
* In: the existing `apps/e2e/tests/Unit/E2E/PestSetupTest.php` subprocess fixtures and maintained Pest setup recovery guidance.
* Out: the pinned Pest version or patch contents, dependency upgrades, TIA selection and cache recovery, bootstrap scheduling, caller database isolation, and live worktree repair.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The native setup hook produces the exact manifest-patched files and exits zero with a writable temporary directory outside Git, at a repository root, and below a real checkout or linked-worktree root, including paths with spaces. Proof: extend `PestSetupTest.php` with isolated Git repositories and upstream package fixtures, and execute them through the E2E affected TIA command.
- [ ] Patch application changes only the selected project's intended Pest installation and setup lock; another project's package, Composer lock files, and tracked and untracked sentinel files in the temporary directory's enclosing repository remain unchanged. Proof: subprocess fixture assertions compare those files and the enclosing repository's HEAD, index, and status before and after setup.
- [ ] An installation left at exact upstream hashes by a failed patch attempt can complete through the native setup hook without deleting or reinstalling dependencies, and repeated setup preserves the verified patched files. Proof: retained-upstream and repeated-run cases in `PestSetupTest.php` verify exit codes, all manifest hashes, and unchanged unrelated files.
- [ ] A nonzero patch command or an exit-zero command that leaves the package at upstream hashes fails setup with an actionable patch-execution diagnostic, without claiming that unchanged package files require reinstalling. Proof: isolated failing and no-op Git process fixtures assert nonzero setup, retained upstream hashes, and the distinction from a modified-package diagnostic.
- [ ] Existing refusal of unsupported versions, changed patch checksums, modified package files, and linked upstream Pest checkouts remains intact, while supported already-patched and no-Pest installations still succeed. Proof: preserve and extend the corresponding `PestSetupTest.php` safety and compatibility cases through the E2E affected TIA command.
- [ ] Contributor guidance explains how to distinguish a patch-execution failure from modified package files and retry through supported setup commands without unnecessary reinstall or cache deletion. Proof: review the setup section in `docs/reference/implementation-loop.md` against the subprocess cases and run `composer docs-lint`.
